raw_response:
The plot is a line chart illustrating the relationship between accuracy (ACC, in percentage) and co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," ranges from 0 to 10^3 (i.e., 1,000) and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 0, 10^1 (10), 10^2 (100), and 10^3 (1,000). The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", ranges from 40 to 65 with linear spacing and tick marks every 5 units. Six data series are presented, each with a distinct color and marker: Base (black circles), MEND (brown diamonds), FT (blue triangles), MEMIT (purple inverted triangles), IKE (red upward-pointing triangles), and ROME (green squares). All lines show an increasing trend as co-occurrence number increases. The Base line starts at approximately 38% ACC and rises to about 43% at 10^3. The FT line begins at around 40% and reaches about 47%. The IKE line starts at 43% and ends at approximately 49%. The MEMIT line begins at 44% and increases to about 54%. The MEND line starts at 44% and reaches approximately 56%. The ROME line starts at 51% and rises to 66% at 10^3, showing the steepest and highest increase among all series.
